blogPosts.title: How Much Does Garden Maintenance Cost in Burwood in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Find out what garden maintenance really costs in Burwood VIC. We break down pricing by garden size, service frequency, and specific needs for Melbourne's eastern suburbs.
body: If you are a Burwood homeowner wondering what garden maintenance costs in 2026, you are not alone. With Melbourne's eastern suburbs experiencing another year of variable weather, keeping your outdoor space in top condition has never been more important — or more confusing when it comes to pricing. At Leaftop, we have been maintaining gardens in Burwood since 2005, and we understand that every property is different. The cost of garden maintenance depends on several factors including the size of your garden, the frequency of visits, and the specific services you require. In this guide, we break down typical pricing for Burwood garden maintenance so you can budget with confidence and avoid overpaying for subpar service.

The size of your garden is the single biggest factor affecting the cost of maintenance in Burwood. A standard suburban block in areas like Burwood East or near Burwood Highway typically features a front and back garden totalling between 200 and 600 square metres of lawn and garden bed. Smaller properties under 200 square metres generally fall into our Essential Lawn Care tier, starting from $65 per visit. Medium-sized Burwood gardens between 200 and 400 square metres suit our Full Garden Service at $120 per visit, which covers mowing, edging, hedge trimming, and weed control. Larger properties over 400 square metres or those requiring intensive seasonal work may need a customised quote from our team.

Frequency of service is another critical factor in determining your garden maintenance costs in Burwood. Melbourne's growing season runs from September through April, during which most Burwood gardens need mowing every two to three weeks to stay healthy and presentable. During winter months from May to August, growth slows significantly and many homeowners opt for monthly visits or fortnightly check-ins. At Leaftop, we offer flexible scheduling that adapts to your garden's needs throughout the year. Our Burwood clients who commit to regular scheduled visits benefit from priority booking during peak season and consistent pricing that does not fluctuate with demand. We always recommend starting with an on-site assessment to determine the ideal frequency for your specific property.

Beyond basic lawn mowing, Burwood homeowners often require additional services that affect the overall cost. Hedge trimming is particularly popular in Burwood's established suburbs where many properties feature mature privet, lilly pilli, or conifer hedges along boundary fences. Mulching is another common request, especially during spring when garden beds need replenishing after winter. Weed control is essential in Burwood's clay-heavy soils where invasive species like oxalis and bindii thrive. At Leaftop, we bundle these services into our Full Garden Service package for maximum value, but we can also provide standalone quotes for any individual service. Transparency is our promise — you will always know exactly what you are paying for before we begin any work.

Many Burwood residents also ask about one-off garden clean-ups, which are ideal for properties that have been neglected or are being prepared for sale. Burwood's property market is competitive, and a well-maintained garden can significantly boost curb appeal and resale value. A comprehensive one-off clean-up typically includes complete garden bed clearing, lawn restoration, hedge reshaping, green waste removal, and fresh mulching. Prices for one-off clean-ups in Burwood generally range from $350 to $800 depending on the scope of work and the volume of green waste. At Leaftop, we provide detailed quotes before starting any one-off project so there are no surprises on the day. Our team arrives fully equipped and ready to transform your garden in a single visit.

When choosing a garden maintenance provider in Burwood, always look for transparent pricing, proper insurance, and local experience. Unfortunately, the gardening industry attracts operators who provide vague quotes and cut corners on quality. At Leaftop, we have been maintaining Burwood gardens for over 20 years and we stand behind every job with a satisfaction guarantee. Our pricing is fixed upfront — we quote once and honour that price regardless of how long the job takes. If you would like an accurate, no-obligation quote for your Burwood property, call us on 1800 001 976 or visit our website. We provide free on-site assessments throughout Burwood, Glen Waverley, Mount Waverley, and surrounding eastern suburbs.

blogPosts.title: When Should You Mow Your Lawn in Melbourne's Eastern Suburbs?
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn the best times to mow your lawn in Burwood and Melbourne's east. A seasonal mowing guide from Leaftop's experienced garden maintenance team.
body: Knowing when to mow your lawn in Melbourne's eastern suburbs like Burwood is one of the most important aspects of garden maintenance, yet it is frequently misunderstood. Melbourne's temperate climate creates a unique growing pattern that differs significantly from northern Australia or even regional Victoria. The key to a healthy, lush lawn in Burwood is understanding the seasonal growth cycles and adjusting your mowing schedule accordingly. At Leaftop, we have maintained lawns across Burwood for over 20 years and we have observed firsthand how Melbourne's unpredictable weather affects grass growth from year to year. In this guide, we share our professional insights on the best times to mow your lawn throughout the year in Burwood and surrounding eastern suburbs.

Spring, from September to November, is when Burwood lawns truly come alive after the cool winter months. As temperatures rise and rainfall increases, cool-season grasses like ryegrass and fescue — which are common throughout Melbourne's east — begin rapid growth. This is the time when most Burwood homeowners need to increase their mowing frequency to every seven to ten days. Cutting too early in spring before the soil has warmed can damage shallow root systems, so we recommend waiting until consistent daytime temperatures reach 15 degrees Celsius. At Leaftop, we monitor soil conditions across our Burwood properties and advise clients on the optimal week to begin their spring mowing schedule. A well-timed first mow sets the tone for the entire growing season.

Summer mowing in Burwood requires a careful balance between maintaining appearance and protecting grass from heat stress. Melbourne's summer temperatures regularly exceed 35 degrees, and Burwood's clay soils can dry out and crack during extended hot spells. The golden rule of summer mowing is to never remove more than one-third of the grass blade in a single cut. This means adjusting your mower height upward during heatwaves to leave grass longer, which shades the soil and retains moisture. Many Burwood lawns feature tall fescue or kikuyu blends that handle Melbourne summers reasonably well, but even hardy varieties suffer when mowed too short in extreme heat. Leaftop adjusts mowing heights automatically as part of our Full Garden Service, keeping Burwood lawns healthy through every summer.

Autumn in Burwood, from March to May, presents another critical window for lawn care. As temperatures cool and rainfall picks up, grass growth resumes after the summer slowdown. This is the ideal time to apply winter grass pre-emergent treatments, which prevent unsightly winter grass weeds from taking over your lawn. Mowing frequency can be adjusted back to every ten to fourteen days as growth moderates. Many Burwood homeowners overlook autumn as a maintenance season, but the work you do in March and April directly determines how your lawn looks come spring. At Leaftop, our autumn service includes soil testing, fertiliser application, and a mowing regime tailored to your grass type. We help Burwood residents prepare their lawns for the quieter winter months ahead.

Winter mowing in Burwood from June to August is minimal but still important. Cool-season grasses continue slow growth during Melbourne's mild winters, and letting grass grow too long can promote fungal diseases like brown patch, which thrives in Burwood's damp winter conditions. Most Burwood lawns need mowing only once every three to four weeks during winter, with the mower set to a higher-than-average cutting height. This is also the time to address drainage issues in low-lying areas of your garden where waterlogging can damage turf. Leaftop's winter garden maintenance visits include lawn assessment, light mowing, and recommendations for any drainage or aeration work that will improve your Burwood lawn's health heading into spring.

Regardless of the season, the quality of your mowing equipment and technique matters enormously. Dull mower blades tear grass rather than cutting it cleanly, leaving brown, ragged edges that invite disease. Burwood's humid conditions, especially during spring and autumn, make clean cuts even more critical for preventing fungal infection. At Leaftop, we service and sharpen our commercial mowing equipment weekly to ensure every Burwood lawn receives a precise, clean cut. If you are unsure about the best mowing schedule for your Burwood property, we offer free lawn assessments where our experienced team evaluates your grass type, soil condition, and garden layout. Call 1800 001 976 to book your free Burwood lawn assessment today.

blogPosts.title: How to Prepare Your Burwood Garden for Melbourne's Wet Winter
blogPosts.excerpt: Get your Burwood garden winter-ready with our comprehensive guide. Soil prep, mulching, lawn care, and planting tips from Leaftop's local experts.
body: Preparing your Burwood garden for Melbourne's winter is essential to ensure it survives the cold, wet months and returns stronger in spring. Burwood sits in Melbourne's eastern suburbs at an elevation that can experience slightly cooler overnight temperatures than coastal areas, making winter preparation even more important for local gardeners. Melbourne winters typically bring temperatures between 5 and 14 degrees Celsius, regular rainfall, and occasional frosts in low-lying pockets around Burwood. At Leaftop, we have prepared thousands of Burwood gardens for winter over our 20-plus years of service. This guide covers the essential steps every Burwood homeowner should take to protect their garden, lawn, and outdoor spaces during the cooler months.

The first step in winter preparation is a thorough garden clean-up, which removes dead plant material, fallen leaves, and debris that can harbour pests and diseases over winter. Burwood's mature trees, including many imported deciduous species along residential streets, drop significant leaf litter that can smother lawn and garden beds if left unchecked. Start your winter prep by clearing all fallen leaves from lawns, garden beds, and gutters. Trim back dead or diseased branches from shrubs and perennials, and remove any spent annuals from garden beds. At Leaftop, our seasonal garden clean-up service in Burwood includes complete debris removal, targeted pruning, and disposal of all green waste. A clean garden going into winter is far less likely to develop problems when spring arrives.

Soil preparation is perhaps the most overlooked aspect of winter garden care in Burwood. Burwood's predominantly clay soils tend to become waterlogged during winter rainfall, which suffocates plant roots and creates ideal conditions for root rot. Before winter arrives, aerate your lawn and garden beds to improve drainage and allow oxygen to reach root systems. Adding a quality organic compost or soil conditioner to garden beds before winter helps improve soil structure and provides slow-release nutrients that plants can access during the dormant season. For Burwood lawns, applying a low-nitrogen winter fertiliser in late autumn strengthens root systems without encouraging tender new growth that frost can damage. Leaftop includes soil assessment and treatment in all our Burwood winter preparation packages.

Mulching is one of the most effective ways to protect Burwood gardens during winter. A generous layer of organic mulch — 75 to 100 millimetres deep — insulates soil against temperature fluctuations, suppresses winter weed growth, and retains moisture during drier winter spells. In Burwood, bark mulch, sugar cane mulch, and pea straw are all popular choices, each offering different benefits for different garden styles. For vegetable gardens, which many Burwood residents maintain in their backyards, straw mulch provides excellent insulation for winter crops like garlic, broad beans, and leafy greens. At Leaftop, we source high-quality mulch at competitive prices and apply it professionally across Burwood gardens. Our mulching service ensures even coverage at the correct depth for maximum winter protection.

Lawn care during Melbourne's winter requires a different approach than the busy spring and summer months. Burwood lawns, predominantly featuring ryegrass, fescue, or kikuyu blends, enter a slower growth phase but still need attention. Mow every three to four weeks at a higher cutting height to avoid stressing the grass. Avoid walking on frosted lawns in Burwood's lower-lying areas, as frozen grass blades break easily and can take weeks to recover. If your Burwood lawn has bare patches from summer wear, winter is actually an ideal time to lay new turf in the protected months before spring growth. Leaftop's winter lawn maintenance keeps Burwood properties looking tidy year-round, with visits scheduled around Melbourne's weather patterns for optimal results.

For Burwood homeowners who enjoy winter gardening, this is the perfect season to plant deciduous trees, bare-root fruit trees, and cool-season vegetables. Burwood's climate is well-suited to growing garlic, broad beans, peas, and brassicas during winter months. Many established Burwood gardens feature mature deciduous trees that lose their leaves in autumn, and planting new specimens during their dormant winter period gives them the best chance of establishing strong root systems before spring. Planning your spring garden now also means you can order seeds and seedlings early, avoiding the rush at local nurseries. Leaftop offers garden planning consultations for Burwood residents who want expert advice on seasonal planting and long-term garden design. Contact us on 1800 001 976 to discuss your winter garden plans.

blogPosts.title: Native Plants That Thrive in Burwood's Clay Soil
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the best native plants for Burwood VIC clay soils. A practical guide to low-maintenance, beautiful native gardens from Leaftop's horticultural experts.
body: Choosing the right native plants for Burwood's clay soil is one of the smartest decisions a local gardener can make. Burwood sits within Melbourne's eastern suburbs where clay-heavy soils are the norm, particularly in areas near Burwood Highway and the foothills of the Dandenong Ranges. Clay soil holds moisture well, which is beneficial during dry periods, but it can become waterlogged in winter and baked hard in summer. Many gardeners new to Burwood struggle with plants that fail to thrive because they have selected species unsuited to these challenging soil conditions. At Leaftop, we have extensive experience working with Burwood's clay soils and can recommend native plants that will not just survive but flourish in your specific garden conditions.

One of the best native trees for Burwood clay soils is the Lemon Myrtle, Backhousia citriodora, which thrives in the heavy, moisture-retentive soils found throughout the suburb. This versatile small tree produces fragrant leaves that can be used in cooking and teas, making it a functional and beautiful addition to Burwood gardens. For larger shade trees, the Australian Elm, Ulmus parvifolia, and the Moreton Bay Fig, Ficus macrophylla, handle Burwood's clay soils remarkably well and provide substantial canopy coverage that reduces summer cooling costs for nearby homes. The Indigenous Box, Eucalyptus microcarpa, is another excellent choice for Burwood gardens with space, tolerating both the wet winters and dry summers typical of Melbourne's east.

For shrubs and understorey planting, Burwood's clay soils support several hardy native options that provide colour and habitat for local wildlife. The Kangaroo Paw, Anigozanthos, is arguably Australia's most iconic native flowering plant and thrives in Burwood's conditions when positioned in well-drained spots. Correa, particularly the Reflexa variety, produces beautiful bell-shaped flowers during winter when Burwood gardens need colour most. Lomandra, a tough strappy-leafed plant, is virtually indestructible in clay soils and works brilliantly as a border plant or mass planting. At Leaftop, we use Lomandra extensively in our Burwood garden designs because it handles everything from full sun to deep shade, and its low maintenance requirements make it perfect for busy homeowners.

Ground covers are essential for suppressing weeds and reducing bare soil in Burwood gardens, and many native ground covers perform exceptionally well in clay. Viola hederacea, commonly known as Native Violet, forms a lush carpet of green foliage with delicate purple and white flowers. It thrives in the shaded, moist conditions that Burwood's clay soils create beneath established trees and along north-facing fences. For sunny positions, Dichondra repens, or Kidney Weed, provides dense ground coverage that handles light foot traffic. Both species are far lower maintenance than traditional lawn in Burwood's challenging clay conditions. Leaftop regularly recommends native ground covers as lawn alternatives for Burwood homeowners looking to reduce mowing requirements while maintaining an attractive garden.

Preparing clay soil for native planting requires some upfront work but pays dividends for years. In Burwood, the best approach is to incorporate generous amounts of organic matter — compost, aged manure, or native soil conditioner — into the planting area before installing new natives. Avoid adding gypsum to clay soil for native plantings, as many Australian natives are adapted to heavy soils and do not benefit from the structural changes gypsum produces. Raised garden beds are another effective solution for Burwood gardens with particularly problematic clay, allowing you to create ideal growing conditions above the native soil level. At Leaftop, our garden design service includes comprehensive soil testing and amendment plans tailored to Burwood's specific conditions, ensuring your native plants establish quickly and thrive long-term.

Maintaining native plants in Burwood's clay soils is generally straightforward once they are established. The most critical period is the first twelve months, during which regular watering, weed control, and mulching are essential to help roots penetrate the heavy clay. After establishment, most native plants require minimal ongoing maintenance, making them ideal for Burwood homeowners who want a beautiful garden without intensive weekly care. Avoid using standard fertilisers on natives, as the high phosphorus content can damage native root systems. Instead, use native-specific slow-release fertilisers available at Burwood garden centres. Leaftop offers ongoing native garden maintenance programs specifically designed for Burwood properties, ensuring your native plantings continue to flourish with minimal effort on your part.
